# English and British monarchs — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/english-and-british-monarchs.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/english-and-british-monarchs.ttl`](../decks/english-and-british-monarchs.ttl) · **Cards:** 42 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The 42 monarchs of England from William I (1066), of Great Britain from 1707 and of the United Kingdom from 1801, to Charles III. Front: the monarch's regnal name in English and Swedish; back: the years of the reign, counted from accession rather than coronation, with both periods for the two kings who reigned twice (a single year means the whole reign fell within that year); a note gives the royal house. Disputed claimants (Empress Matilda, Lady Jane Grey) are not counted, William III and Mary II have a card each, and there was no monarch during the Interregnum of 1649–1660. Based on Wikidata and the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (public domain), and checked against the Royal Household's website (royal.uk) and Wikipedia.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0 like most of the library. Its content sources are Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0, and the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica as transcribed on Wikisource, which is in the public domain in the United States (published before 1931). Everything on the cards comes from these two or is the compiler's own documented decision: the selection of monarchs (the holders of the four Wikidata offices from 1066, less the disputed claimants named in the selection), the reign years (P39 start and end times; Stephen's two statements joined into one reign because Matilda is not counted; William III's 1689 start from Wikidata's statement for Mary II, together with William III, and his Wikidata descriptions), the English and Swedish names, the royal houses and their Swedish names (Wikidata P53 and labels; the House of Stuart of James I, Charles II, James II, Mary II and Anne because their Wikidata house, Stewart of Darnley, is part of the House of Stuart; "Huset Blois" and "Huset Sachsen-Coburg-Gotha" the compiler's renderings in the pattern of the Wikidata Swedish house labels), and the facts in the notes (Wikidata statements and items, the first and last of a house and the longest reign computed from them, and the facts listed in the 1911 Britannica's usedFor). From the 1911 Britannica only facts were taken, restated in the compiler's words, with no text copied; it is credited all the same. The Royal Household's website (royal.uk, © Crown Copyright, no open licence, so all rights reserved), the English Wikipedia and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) are verification sources only: they were consulted to confirm the facts the content sources gave and supplied no fact, text, table or selection. Until quality-control round 4 some note facts and the Stuart houses had been taken from royal.uk and the English Wikipedia; round 4 re-sourced each of them to Wikidata or the 1911 Britannica and removed the ones neither states. The selection is the complete set of the office holders, which coincides with any full list of English and British monarchs because it is the complete set, not a choice taken from a list. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence are not part of the CC0 deck: they remain under their sources' terms (Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0, by Wikipedia contributors, each linked to the quoted revision; the Royal Household's text © Crown Copyright, all rights reserved; the 1911 Britannica public domain in the United States) and are short quotations given only to make the verification checkable.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released. Every query, URL and command run is listed under queries; the raw responses were saved in the research scratch directory.
2. Offices: the Wikidata API (query 1) found the four items for the offices the deck covers: Monarch of England (Q18810062), Monarch of Great Britain (Q110324075, 1707–1800), monarch of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (Q111722535, 1801–1927) and Monarch of the United Kingdom (Q9134365, since 1927).
3. Selection and reign years: query 2 listed every non-deprecated position-held (P39) statement for the four offices with its start and end times. The query's filter, a start time in 1066 or later (FILTER(YEAR(?start) >= 1066)), returns 44 people: Harold Godwinson (Q159597), whose statement starts on 6 January 1066 (Julian; the endpoint shows 1066-01-11 after converting to Gregorian), and the 43 holders whose first statement starts on or after William I's accession on 25 December 1066 (Julian). Harold, the last king before the Norman Conquest, was then removed by hand, because the deck starts with the Norman Conquest; the Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings before him are already outside the filter. That left 43 people. Lady Jane Grey (Q162356), who has a P39 statement for July 1553, was left out as a disputed claimant (see the selection), leaving 42 cards. The statements of one person under successive offices were joined into one reign (Anne: England 1702–1707 and Great Britain 1707–1714; George III: Great Britain 1760–1801 and the United Kingdom 1801–1820; George V: 1910–1927 and 1927–1936). Reigns interrupted by another monarch keep both periods (Henry VI, Edward IV). The back gives the years only, start–end with an en dash; a reign that began and ended in the same year is a single year (Edward V, Edward VIII), and the description says so, since in the back-to-front direction "1483" and "1936" are years in which other monarchs also reigned; the reigning monarch's back is open-ended ("2022–").
4. Calendar: Wikidata stores most dates before the British calendar change of 1752 in the Julian calendar (calendar model Q1985786), and the SPARQL endpoint (queries 2 and 23) returns every date converted to the proleptic Gregorian calendar, e.g. William I's start time, stored as 25 December 1066 (Julian), comes back as 1066-12-31. The first version of the dossier quoted the converted dates; in quality-control round 4 every date in the cards' Wikidata evidence was replaced by the value as stored, with its calendar model (Julian or Gregorian), from a fresh wbgetentities download (query 20). No year on any card changes. Some of Wikidata's dates around 1700 are stored as Gregorian although they are the Old Style days (e.g. William III, 28 December 1694); they are quoted as stored.
5. Reign convention: a reign is counted from accession, the moment the previous monarch died, abdicated or was deposed (the Royal Household's accession page: "A new Sovereign succeeds to the throne as soon as his or her predecessor dies"), not from coronation; so Edward V and Edward VIII, who were never crowned, are counted. The convention changes the start year of many reigns (Elizabeth II, for example, acceded on 6 February 1952 and was crowned in 1953); for William I, who came to the throne by conquest, Wikidata's statement starts on 25 December 1066 (Julian), the day of his coronation (the 1911 Britannica), so the year is 1066 either way. Charles II's reign is given from the Restoration in 1660, as Wikidata does (start time 29 May 1660, Julian) and the Royal Household and Wikipedia confirm, with a note that he had taken the title of king on his father's execution in 1649 (the 1911 Britannica).
6. Names: the English front is the regnal name: the Wikidata English or multilingual ("mul") label or alias of the person, or that label with the territorial suffix ("of England", "of Great Britain") removed (query 4; e.g. the mul label "Henry VIII", the en label "John of England" shortened to "John"); the Royal Household's page headings and the English Wikipedia lists write the names the same way (verification). The Swedish front is the established Swedish form: the Wikidata Swedish label or alias with the territorial suffix ("av England", "av Storbritannien") removed, e.g. "Henrik VIII av England" (with the alias "Henrik VIII"), "Vilhelm I av England" (alias), "Johan av England", "Stefan av Blois", "Anna av Storbritannien", "Viktoria av Storbritannien". The Swedish forms translate the given name as Swedish has long done for historical monarchs (Vilhelm, Henrik, Rikard, Johan, Edvard, Maria, Elisabet, Jakob, Karl, Anna, Georg, Viktoria) but keep "Elizabeth II" and "Charles III" untranslated: that is how the Wikidata Swedish labels and the Swedish Wikipedia articles write them ("Elizabeth II av Storbritannien", "Charles III av Storbritannien"). Each Swedish form was checked against the first sentence of the person's Swedish Wikipedia article (query 13), which is quoted in the card's evidence. Nationalencyklopedin and Språkrådet could not be read from the research environment (query 15).
7. Royal houses (the back note): the house is the Wikidata P53 (family) of the monarch (query 3), named by the house item's English label and, in Swedish, its Swedish label (query 5: Normandiska ätten, Huset Plantagenet, Huset Lancaster, Huset York, Huset Tudor, Huset Stuart, Huset Nassau-Oranien, Huset Hannover, Huset Windsor). For James I, Charles II, James II, Mary II and Anne Wikidata's P53 is Q3973466 "House of Stewart di Darnley", which Wikidata has as part of (P361) the House of Stuart (Q179840), Charles I's P53; the notes give the House of Stuart, and the builder checks both statements. Where Wikidata gives several houses (Henry II: Plantagenet, Normandy and Angevins; Henry IV: Lancaster and Plantagenet; Elizabeth II: Windsor, preferred, besides Saxe-Coburg and Gotha and the British royal family; Charles III: Windsor and Glücksburg), the note gives the one the monarch shares with the neighbouring monarchs, or the preferred one; George V's note gives both of his, with Wikidata's 1917 qualifiers. Stephen is of the House of Blois and William III of the House of Orange-Nassau (Wikidata P53). "Huset Sachsen-Coburg-Gotha" is the Wikidata Swedish label "Sachsen-Coburg-Gotha" (Q1753846) with "Huset" prefixed, as in the other Swedish house labels, and is also the Swedish Wikipedia's usage (the category "Huset Sachsen-Coburg-Gotha" on the article on Edvard VII). "Huset Blois" is the compiler's rendering in the same pattern (Q1590002 has no Swedish label), confirmed by Swedish Wikipedia usage (query 14). The Royal Household's house pages and the English Wikipedia lists' sections were consulted to confirm the houses (verification only). Where the Wikidata P53 value is the house the note names, the builder checks it.
8. Cross-check against the Royal Household: the royal.uk sitemap (query 7) gave the URLs of the history pages; the list "Kings and Queens from 1066" and the page of each monarch and house were downloaded (queries 8 and 9). The heading of each monarch's page (e.g. "Henry VI (r.1422-1461 and 1470-1471)") was compared by the dossier script with the card's back: the headings of the 39 monarch pages (William III and Mary II share one) agree with the 40 cards' years. For Elizabeth II and Charles III, which have no such heading, the accession page (6 February 1952), the news items of 8 September 2022 and the Court Circular of 1 October 2026 ("The King and Queen this evening received …") were read; the last confirms that Charles III was still reigning shortly before the deck was made.
9. Independent cross-check: the English Wikipedia lists of English and of British monarchs (query 10) give exact accession and end dates for every card; rows.py printed the name and reign cell of every row, and every card's years agree with them. These lists cite the Royal Household among other references, so they are not wholly independent of it; Britannica and Historic Royal Palaces, the intended independent references, refused the research environment's requests (HTTP 403, query 15). Wikidata's statements, the content source, agree with them except as recorded in quality control (William III's own statement starts in 1694, Stephen's reign is split in two, Mary I's start day).
10. Notes: each back note starts with the royal house and, where it helps the learner, adds a short fact in the compiler's own words. Every such fact comes from a content source: from Wikidata (nicknames as aliases, e.g. "William Rufus"/"Vilhelm Rufus", "Richard the Lionheart"/"Rikard Lejonhjärta", "John I Lackland"/"Johan utan land", "William of Orange", "James VII of Scotland"/"Jakob VII av Skottland"; P39 qualifiers for joint reigns (P1706) and abdications (P1534) and for successors; deaths (P1196, P509, P570); the items Lady Jane Grey Q162356, Empress Matilda Q150872, Magna Carta Q12519, Battle of Bosworth Field Q222013, Princes in the Tower Q648580, Interregnum Q2558636, Stuart Restoration Q846848, Glorious Revolution Q189508, Acts of Union 1707 Q193515, Regency era Q25861 and House of Windsor Q81589; the first and last monarch of a house from the P53 statements, and the longest reign from the P39 statements, query 22; James I as the first holder of both the English and the Scottish crown, query 23), or, where Wikidata does not state it, from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica on Wikisource (query 21; the facts are listed in that source's usedFor). Each is quoted in the card's evidence. The Royal Household and Wikipedia were consulted to confirm them and supplied none. In quality-control round 4 the facts that neither content source states were removed or reworded: Edward V and Edward VIII never crowned (removed), the Royal Household grouping William III with the Stuarts (removed), Charles II's regnal years officially counted from 1649 (now: he took the title of king in 1649), Richard I and John as Angevin kings (now: Henry II counted among the Angevins, from his father's county of Anjou), Richard II "deposed" (now: forced to give up the throne, as Wikidata's abdication and the 1911 Britannica have it) and James II "deposed" (now: lost the throne in the Glorious Revolution).
11. Study direction: every back is unique (the builder checks this), and asking for the monarch from the reign years makes sense, so the deck is bidirectional.
12. The dossier was written by a script (build_dossier.py) from the saved responses and a hand-written table of the cards (cards_data.py), so that every quoted Wikidata value, royal.uk heading and Swedish Wikipedia sentence is copied from the saved data and asserted to be verbatim; the builder then ran its Wikidata checks against live Wikidata (query 17).
13. Helper scripts: the research used small Python scripts in the research scratch directory, which are not published with the deck; what each did: wd.py ran Wikidata API searches, SPARQL queries (POST to https://query.wikidata.org/sparql, retrying on HTTP 429/5xx) and entity downloads and saved the JSON responses; sitemap.py downloaded the three royal.uk sitemap pages and printed the URLs whose path names a monarch, a house or the history pages; royal.py downloaded royal.uk pages, saved the HTML and reduced the <main> element to plain text (scripts and styles removed, tags stripped, whitespace collapsed); wiki.py fetched Wikipedia articles through the MediaWiki API (revision id, wikitext and plain-text introduction); rows.py printed the section headings and the name-and-reign cell of every table row in the two English Wikipedia lists' wikitext, with references and footnote templates removed; cards_data.py is the hand-written table of the cards (fronts, backs, notes, which page and row each card's evidence quotes), and build_dossier.py assembled the dossier from it and the saved responses, asserting that every quoted value occurs verbatim in the saved data. Split P39 statements of one person were merged by hand in cards_data.py, as step 2 describes. In quality-control round 3 the name part of each card's Wikidata evidence was rewritten from a fresh wbgetentities download (query 18) by a further script, which states which label or alias the card text is, or which one it shortens. In quality-control round 4: fetch.py downloaded the full entities (wbgetentities: labels, aliases, descriptions, claims) of the 42 monarchs and of the house, office and event items; show.py printed selected statements with their qualifiers, times as stored and calendar models; search.py ran wbsearchentities and label lookups; ws.py fetched 1911 Britannica articles from Wikisource (parse API: revision id and rendered text, tags stripped) and grep.py printed passages from them; patch4.py rewrote the dossier, asserting that every 1911 Britannica quotation occurs verbatim in the saved text and generating the Wikidata dates from the saved entities.

## Selection

All monarchs of England from William I (1066) to the union with Scotland, of Great Britain from 1707 and of the United Kingdom from 1801 to the present, Charles III: the holders of the four Wikidata offices from 1066, 42 people with a card each. The deck starts at 1066 because the brief is the post-Conquest monarchy (the Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, Harold Godwinson and Edgar Ætheling are left out). Left out as disputed claimants, whom the English Wikipedia lists under "Disputed claimant": Empress Matilda (in 1141; the Royal Household treats her with Stephen, 1135–1154, and Wikidata has no office statement for her), Louis of France (1216–1217) and Lady Jane Grey (proclaimed 10 July 1553, deposed 19 July; the Royal Household lists her, "Lady Jane Grey (r. 10-19 July 1553)", and says "six if Lady Jane Grey is included" of the Tudors, Wikidata has an office statement for her, but the English Wikipedia lists her as a disputed claimant, and her nine days are not counted as a reign in this deck): she is mentioned in the note on Mary I. William III and Mary II, joint monarchs from 1689, have a card each with their own years (1689–1702 and 1689–1694), as the Royal Household gives them. The Interregnum (1649–1660, the Commonwealth and the Protectorate of Oliver and Richard Cromwell) had no monarch and has no card; it is mentioned in the notes on Charles I and Charles II. Edward V (1483) and Edward VIII (1936), who reigned but were never crowned, are included, since a reign is counted from accession. The monarchs of Scotland before 1603 and of Ireland are not included, except as the same people (James I, also James VI of Scotland). Charles III's reign is open-ended, as of 4 October 2026.

## Queries

**1. Find the Wikidata items of the four offices (Wikidata API wbsearchentities, run through the helper wd.py with the User-Agent above)** (Wikidata: the holders of the offices Monarch of England (Q18810062), Monarch of Great Britain (Q110324075), monarch of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (Q111722535) and Monarch of the United Kingdom (Q9134365), their position-held statements (P39) with start and end times and qualifiers, their royal houses (P53), their English and Swedish labels, aliases and descriptions, and the items for the houses and the events named in the notes)

```
https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities&search=monarch+of+England&language=en&format=json&limit=8
https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities&search=monarch+of+Great+Britain&language=en&format=json&limit=8
https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities&search=monarch+of+the+United+Kingdom&language=en&format=json&limit=8
```

**2. Every non-deprecated P39 (position held) statement for the four offices — Monarch of England (Q18810062), Monarch of Great Britain (Q110324075), monarch of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (Q111722535), Monarch of the United Kingdom (Q9134365) — with start and end times, predecessor and successor qualifiers and English and Swedish labels (POST to https://query.wikidata.org/sparql; raw JSON saved as q1.json)** (Wikidata: the holders of the offices Monarch of England (Q18810062), Monarch of Great Britain (Q110324075), monarch of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (Q111722535) and Monarch of the United Kingdom (Q9134365), their position-held statements (P39) with start and end times and qualifiers, their royal houses (P53), their English and Swedish labels, aliases and descriptions, and the items for the houses and the events named in the notes)

```
SELECT ?person ?en ?sv ?position ?start ?end ?rank ?replaces ?replacedBy WHERE {
  VALUES ?position { wd:Q18810062 wd:Q110324075 wd:Q111722535 wd:Q9134365 }
  ?person p:P39 ?st .
  ?st ps:P39 ?position ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
  FILTER(?rank != wikibase:DeprecatedRank)
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P582 ?end }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P1365 ?replaces }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P1366 ?replacedBy }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?start ?position
```

**3. A first version of the house and sitelink query, with GROUP BY and ORDER BY MIN(?start), was rejected by the endpoint (HTTP 400): it is not repeated here. The query run instead: the royal house (P53, all ranks) with English and Swedish labels and the Swedish Wikipedia sitelink of every office holder from 1066 (saved as q2.json)** (Wikidata: the holders of the offices Monarch of England (Q18810062), Monarch of Great Britain (Q110324075), monarch of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (Q111722535) and Monarch of the United Kingdom (Q9134365), their position-held statements (P39) with start and end times and qualifiers, their royal houses (P53), their English and Swedish labels, aliases and descriptions, and the items for the houses and the events named in the notes)

```
SELECT DISTINCT ?person ?en ?sv ?house ?houseEn ?houseSv ?houseRank ?svwiki WHERE {
  VALUES ?position { wd:Q18810062 wd:Q110324075 wd:Q111722535 wd:Q9134365 }
  ?person p:P39 ?st .
  ?st ps:P39 ?position ; pq:P580 ?start .
  FILTER(YEAR(?start) >= 1066)
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?person p:P53 ?hst . ?hst ps:P53 ?house ; wikibase:rank ?houseRank .
    OPTIONAL { ?house rdfs:label ?houseEn FILTER(LANG(?houseEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?house rdfs:label ?houseSv FILTER(LANG(?houseSv) = "sv") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?svwiki schema:about ?person ; schema:isPartOf <https://sv.wikipedia.org/> }
}
```

**4. All English, Swedish and multilingual (mul) labels and aliases of the office holders from 1066, for the card names and the label checks (saved as q3.json)** (Wikidata: the holders of the offices Monarch of England (Q18810062), Monarch of Great Britain (Q110324075), monarch of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (Q111722535) and Monarch of the United Kingdom (Q9134365), their position-held statements (P39) with start and end times and qualifiers, their royal houses (P53), their English and Swedish labels, aliases and descriptions, and the items for the houses and the events named in the notes)

```
SELECT ?person ?kind ?lang ?text WHERE {
  VALUES ?position { wd:Q18810062 wd:Q110324075 wd:Q111722535 wd:Q9134365 }
  ?person p:P39 ?st .
  ?st ps:P39 ?position ; pq:P580 ?start .
  FILTER(YEAR(?start) >= 1066)
  VALUES (?kind ?pred) { ("label" rdfs:label) ("alias" skos:altLabel) }
  ?person ?pred ?text .
  BIND(LANG(?text) AS ?lang)
  FILTER(?lang IN ("en", "sv", "mul"))
}
ORDER BY ?person ?lang ?kind
```

**22. Quality control round 4: the total length of each person's P39 statements for the four offices (SPARQL, POST to https://query.wikidata.org/sparql via wd.py), for Elizabeth II as the longest-reigning** (Wikidata: the holders of the offices Monarch of England (Q18810062), Monarch of Great Britain (Q110324075), monarch of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (Q111722535) and Monarch of the United Kingdom (Q9134365), their position-held statements (P39) with start and end times and qualifiers, their royal houses (P53), their English and Swedish labels, aliases and descriptions, and the items for the houses and the events named in the notes)

```
SELECT ?person ?personLabel (SUM(?days) AS ?total) WHERE {
  VALUES ?position { wd:Q18810062 wd:Q110324075 wd:Q111722535 wd:Q9134365 }
  ?person p:P39 ?st .
  ?st ps:P39 ?position ; pq:P580 ?start .
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?st wikibase:rank wikibase:DeprecatedRank }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P582 ?end0 }
  BIND(COALESCE(?end0, NOW()) AS ?end)
  BIND(xsd:integer(?end - ?start) AS ?days)
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
}
GROUP BY ?person ?personLabel
ORDER BY DESC(?total)
LIMIT 8
```

**23. Quality control round 4: holders of both Monarch of England and Monarch of Scotland, by first English start (SPARQL via wd.py), for James I as the first monarch of both** (Wikidata: the holders of the offices Monarch of England (Q18810062), Monarch of Great Britain (Q110324075), monarch of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (Q111722535) and Monarch of the United Kingdom (Q9134365), their position-held statements (P39) with start and end times and qualifiers, their royal houses (P53), their English and Swedish labels, aliases and descriptions, and the items for the houses and the events named in the notes)

```
SELECT ?person ?personLabel (MIN(?start) AS ?firstEngland) WHERE {
  ?person p:P39 ?st .
  ?st ps:P39 wd:Q18810062 ; pq:P580 ?start .
  ?person wdt:P39 wd:Q12716207 .
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
}
GROUP BY ?person ?personLabel
ORDER BY ?firstEngland
```

## Quality control

7 rounds, 30 findings: 21 fixed, 2 rejected after checking, 7 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (195 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's reign against Wikidata's P39 statements, the Royal Household's page headings and the English Wikipedia lists; the Swedish names against Wikidata labels and the Swedish Wikipedia; the houses against the Royal Household's house pages, Wikidata P53 and the English Wikipedia; the contested cases. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 42 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

The Royal Household's headings and the English Wikipedia lists agree on the years of all 42 reigns, and the Swedish Wikipedia introductions agree wherever they give the years; Wikidata agrees except for William III's start (1694 for 1689) and the split of Stephen's reign, where the cards follow the better sources and no check depends on the Wikidata value. The contested cases were decided as the selection explains (Matilda, Louis and Lady Jane Grey left out; William III and Mary II a card each; no card for the Interregnum; Edward V and Edward VIII counted from accession). The brief's Swedish "Karl III" was replaced by the established "Charles III". Builder checks cover every front in both languages, every office and most houses.

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 42 cards: every reign against a live Wikidata SPARQL query of the P39 statements of the four offices, an independent web list of reign years and the Royal Household's pages; the notes; recency of Charles III's reign (Court Circular of 1 October 2026); the Swedish names against Wikidata.

No factual errors; the count of 42 and the coverage hold, and the round-0 resolutions (William III 1689–1702, Stephen as one reign, Mary I after Lady Jane Grey, Charles III in Swedish) were confirmed. One warning on William III's house and one suggestion on single-year backs in the back-to-front direction; both applied after checking the Royal Household's Stuart page (query 19).

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| william-iii | The note gave only the House of Orange-Nassau, while the Royal Household, the deck's authority for houses, lists William III among the Stuarts (and the English Wikipedia list files him under "Houses of Stuart and Orange"); Mary II's card gives the House of Stuart for the same joint reign. | Verified on https://www.royal.uk/stuarts (fetched 2026-10-04): its list of Stuart monarchs includes "William III (r. 1689-1702) and Mary II (r. 1689-1694)"; Wikidata P53 of Q129987 is Q155483 House of Orange-Nassau (sv label "Huset Nassau-Oranien"). The note now gives both: en "House of Orange-Nassau (the Royal Household lists him with the Stuarts). …", sv "Huset Nassau-Oranien (det brittiska kungahuset räknar honom till huset Stuart). …"; the P53 check is kept and the Stuart page's list is quoted in the evidence. | fixed |
| edward-v | In the back-to-front direction the prompt "1483" (and "1936" for Edward VIII) has a unique answer only by the deck's convention that a single year means the whole reign fell within it, since Edward IV and Richard III also reigned in 1483 and George V and George VI in 1936; the convention was stated in the method only. | Verified against the Wikidata P39 dates. The convention is now stated in the description in both languages ("a single year means the whole reign fell within that year" / "ett enda årtal betyder att hela regeringstiden föll inom det året"), which the learner sees for the whole deck, and the method says why. Applies equally to edward-viii; the cards themselves are unchanged. | fixed |

The royal.uk licence evidence now quotes the © Crown Copyright footer, the Swedish house-name method is corrected, the Wikidata evidence of every card now says exactly which label or alias the card text is or shortens (fresh download, query 18), and the helper scripts are described. Two suggestions declined or partly applied as recorded.

One error: royal.uk (all rights reserved) and the English Wikipedia (CC BY-SA), both verification sources, had supplied facts to the CC0 deck (the Stuart house of five monarchs, William III's 1689 start, Stephen's single reign, facts in the notes), which the licence policy forbids. Fixed by re-sourcing every such fact to Wikidata or to a new public-domain content source, the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica on Wikisource, and by removing or rewording the few that neither states; the deck stays CC0. One warning: the Wikidata dates quoted in the evidence were the SPARQL endpoint's Gregorian conversions; every date is now quoted as stored, with its calendar model, and the round-0 William I finding is corrected. Both suggestions applied (George V's house note; "interregnumet").

### Round 5: Re-check of changed cards and a sample (facts, language, documentation) (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent re-check reviewer · **Scope:** All 42 cards (all changed in round 4) against royal.uk's list, live Wikidata P39 statements and Swedish labels, and six 1911 Britannica quotations re-fetched from Wikisource; the method against the queries it cites; the licensing decision; the .ttl and .md against the dossier.
